assumptions: all words of length <= 10 (<= 8 for the doubling rules)
meta.falsification: A random-descent word with g != D mod 2; a word whose Grundy value differs from the XOR of run values; a Grundy value >= 4.
meta.hypothesis: H-C04-4: for random-descent rules g(w) = D(w) mod 2 (D the unique derivation length), so P-positions are exactly the words with even D (for ab -> ba: an even number of inversions). H-C04-5: for a rule a^k -> u the game is the disjoint sum of a take-and-break game on the maximal a-runs, g(w) = XOR over runs of G(run length). H-C04-6 (bold): every rewriting game in the family has Grundy values <= 3 on words of length <= 10.
meta.methodology: Grundy values by mex over the exact derivation graph. For unary left-hand sides the run game G is computed independently from its definition (heap n, rewrite position i, resulting heaps i + e_0, e_1, ..., n - k - i + e_t from the a-blocks e_j of u).
meta.question: What do the Sprague-Grundy values of rewriting games look like?
